questions.q: Chloroacetone (CH₃COCH₂Cl) is treated with aqueous NaOH and the mixture is then acidified. The organic product is:
questions.explain: This is a Favorskii rearrangement: the enolate on the CH₃ side closes a cyclopropanone by intramolecular SN2, OH⁻ adds to its C=O and the ring opens to give propanoate, which acid work-up converts to propanoic acid. Simple substitution to hydroxyacetone is the trap.

questions.q: 2-Chlorocyclohexanone is heated with sodium methoxide in methanol. The major product is:
questions.explain: The cyclic α-halo ketone undergoes a Favorskii rearrangement with ring contraction: the C=O carbon is pushed out of the ring and becomes the ester carbon, so the six-membered ring becomes a five-membered one. With an alkoxide the product is an ester rather than an acid.

questions.q: Which α-halo ketone CANNOT give the cyclopropanone intermediate needed for a normal Favorskii rearrangement?
questions.explain: A cyclopropanone needs at least one hydrogen on the α′-carbon, on the other side of the C=O from the halogen. In C₆H₅C(CH₃)₂COCH₂Cl that carbon is quaternary, so exam answers show plain SN2 substitution to C₆H₅C(CH₃)₂COCH₂OH instead.

questions.q: 1,3-Dichlorobutan-2-one (ClCH₂COCHClCH₃) is treated with OH⁻ followed by H₃O⁺. The product is:
questions.explain: The cyclopropanone formed still carries one chlorine. When the ring opens, the carbanion expels that chloride and forms a C=C bond conjugated with the carboxyl group, giving the α,β-unsaturated acid but-2-enoic acid.
